Ask Verse, the site assistant#

Ask Verse is the button at the bottom-right of the product page, the app, Studio and these docs. Type what you want in your own words — it answers in a sentence or two and, where it can, does it for you by pressing the page's own controls.

You need: nothing. It works on day one without any setup, in basic mode. An operator can switch on AI mode with one environment variable (see Operator setup).

What you can ask#

Say something likeWhat happens
"I want to show my apartment model to a client"Opens the app and the upload panel
"How big can my file be?"Answers, and shows the current limits card
"Open a demo scene"Loads one of the public demo scenes
"Walk through this" · "Back to orbit"Switches walk mode on or off
"Play the tour" · "Stop the tour"Plays or stops the scene's automatic camera tour
"Make a video of this"Opens the Export video options
"Share this scene"Shows the scene link and copies it
"Collect comments on it"Turns on review mode
"Make it private"Takes you to Studio and says which control to use
"Embed this on my site"Opens the embed guide
"Take me to the Blender exporter"Opens that guide
"Show me around"Starts the guided tour of the page
"How much does it cost?"Points you to hello@ctruh.com

Each thing it does appears under the reply as a small chip ("Switched to walk mode"), with Undo or Back where that makes sense. The conversation follows you when the assistant moves you to another page, and is forgotten when you close the tab.

Keyboard: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, Esc closes the panel. On a phone the panel is a full-height sheet.

What it cannot do#

  • It cannot upload a file for you, sign in, or see or change your account, tokens or scenes. Making a scene private or revoking a link is done by you, in Studio.
  • It only ever performs actions from a short fixed list (below), on this site. It cannot open other websites.
  • It answers questions about using Verse Engine and nothing else.
  • Rendering quality has no in-page menu, so it cannot change it — it opens Tune quality knobs instead.

The complete list of actions:

ActionDoes
navigateGoes to /, /app, /studio, /docs/ or a section of the product page
open_uploadOpens the upload panel / file picker in the app
load_demoOpens a public demo scene
start_tourStarts the guided product tour of a page
set_viewWalk, orbit, play or stop the scene tour, toggle the minimap or the measure tool
export_videoOpens the video export options
open_reviewTurns on review mode
share_linkShows and copies the scene link
open_docsOpens a public documentation page
show_limitsShows the upload limits

Every action is checked against this list twice: by the server before it is sent, and by the page before it runs. Anything else is dropped.

Basic mode and AI mode#

  • Basic (the default): the server matches your request against a curated set of common tasks and searches the headings of these docs. Nothing leaves the server.
  • AI: the server sends the conversation to Anthropic's Claude API and streams the reply back. The model is given the public guides and the current limits, and can only answer with text plus the actions above.

The small tag beside the panel title says which mode is on. If the AI service is unreachable, that one reply falls back to basic mode.

Privacy#

  • In AI mode, the messages you type (and which page you are on, and whether a scene is loaded) are sent to Anthropic's API to generate the reply. Do not type passwords or account tokens — the assistant never needs them.
  • Verse does not store your messages. The server logs one line per request with counts only (message count, characters, latency, token usage) — never the text. The conversation lives in your browser tab's session storage and is gone when the tab closes.
  • In basic mode nothing is sent to any third party.

Turning it off#

Add ?assistant=0 to any page URL to hide the button. It never appears inside an embedded viewer (embed.html) or any iframe.

Operator setup#

The assistant needs no configuration. To enable AI mode on a server you run, set:

VariableDefaultMeaning
ANTHROPIC_API_KEYunsetSet it to switch on AI mode. Unset = basic mode.
VERSE_ASSIST_MODELclaude-haiku-4-5The Claude model. The default is the fast, inexpensive tier, which suits navigation help.
VERSE_ASSIST_DAILY_CAP1000Most AI requests answered per UTC day, across all visitors. Past it the endpoint answers 503 with a friendly message until the next day (or a restart).
VERSE_ASSIST_PER_HOUR40Messages per hour per IP address, both modes.
VERSE_ASSIST_MAX_TOKENS700Longest reply, in output tokens.

Other built-in limits: 20 messages per conversation, 1,000 characters per message, 3 actions per reply, a 25-second timeout, and at most 8 replies being written at once. GET /v1/assist/status reports the mode; the endpoint itself is documented in the API reference.

Cost, as a rough guide: the product knowledge sent with every request is cached on Anthropic's side, so a typical exchange on the default model costs a fraction of a US cent. The daily cap is the hard ceiling.
